# Phase 1 — encoder speed: presets + multithreaded planning

> Era note: this run predates release. "v4" here is the shipped **v1**
> bitstream (only the version byte was renumbered 4→1; wire otherwise
> identical); "pack"/`--no-joint` refer to the removed v3 archive mode —
> the LPC/Rice core measured is the same one in v1.

Build: working tree on top of `9f25157` (Phase 1 changes: `EncodeOpts`,
presets `-0/-5/-8`, `-j N`). v3 wire format and decoder unchanged.
Machine: 24 logical CPUs, Windows. Corpus: the same 47-file common subset as
`2026-10-22_e254a5b.md` (668.1 MiB WAV/AIFF, every reference tool accepted).
Encode wall time per file via `subprocess` + `perf_counter`; FLAC/WavPack =
min of 3 runs, FLQ = 1 run. All FLQ runs `--no-joint` unless stated (the v4
target path: LPC/Rice + stereo modes, no references).

## Reference baseline (honest thread counts)

| Tool | Output | Encode | Throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| FLAC 1.5.0 -8 -j1 | 51.15% | 9.89 s | 67.6 MiB/s |
| FLAC 1.5.0 -8 -j8 | 51.15% | 2.34 s | 285.7 MiB/s |
| WavPack 5.9.0 -hx | 52.04% | 12.06 s | 55.4 MiB/s |
| FLQ pre-Phase-1, `--no-joint` (1 thread) | 50.77% | 153.4 s | 4.35 MiB/s |
| FLQ pre-Phase-1, full (1 thread) | 50.51% | 461.8 s | 1.45 MiB/s |

The earlier "4–80x slower" figure compared single-threaded FLQ with
`flac -j8`; at equal thread count the pre-Phase-1 gap was ~15x.

## Presets

Preset only changes encoder decisions (LPC order search); every output is a
normal v3 file, decoded bit-exact.

- `-8` — exhaustive: every order in {1,2,4,8,12,16,24,32} fully evaluated
  (pre-Phase-1 behavior; byte-identical output on all 47 files).
- `-5` (default) — each order is quantized to its real 15-bit coefficients and
  scored by mean |residual| on every 2nd sample; only the 2 best are fully
  Rice-planned (plus order 0).
- `-0` — same with every 4th sample and only the best one.

| FLQ `--no-joint` | Output | Δ vs -8 | Worst file Δ | 1 thread | 8 threads | 24 threads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -8 | 50.77% | — | — | 4.46 MiB/s | — | — |
| -5 | 50.77% | +0.004 pp | +0.033 pp | 8.80 MiB/s | 30.8 MiB/s | 32.4 MiB/s |
| -0 | 50.79% | +0.019 pp | +0.083 pp | 12.45 MiB/s | 37.8 MiB/s | — |

Gate (default preset ≤ +0.15 pp vs exhaustive): **passed** (+0.004 pp).

### Rejected first attempt

Ranking orders by the Levinson prediction error (`0.5·n·log2(err) + order·15`)
cost +0.48 pp in aggregate and up to +9.8 pp on narrowband radio recordings:
it favoured orders 24/32 whose quantized coefficients predict badly (−8 picked
order 12 on 582 of 617 signals of the worst file; the estimate never evaluated
it). A neighbour-climb from the estimate still left +4.7/+6.5 pp on two files
(non-unimodal cost curve). Scoring with the quantized coefficients fixed it.

## Where this leaves speed

| At equal threads | FLQ -5 `--no-joint` | FLAC -8 | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 thread | 8.80 MiB/s | 67.6 MiB/s | 7.7x |
| 8 threads | 30.8 MiB/s | 285.7 MiB/s | 9.3x |

FLQ got 2.0x faster at 1 thread (4.35 → 8.80 MiB/s) and 7.4x with all
cores (4.35 → 32.4 MiB/s), at an
unchanged ratio that is still below FLAC -8 (50.77% vs 51.15%). It remains
roughly an order of magnitude slower than FLAC at equal thread count.
Thread scaling flattens past 8 (sequential per-file work: parse, CRC,
bitstream write, the per-block pass that consumes the parallel plans).

Joint analysis (`flq encode` without `--no-joint`, the v3 archive path) is
still sequential and dominates encode time there; Phase 1 did not touch it.

Repro: `python D:\TEMP\flq_ab\timing.py <flq.exe> <tag> [flq flags]`
(outside the repo by policy); CSVs in `D:\TEMP\flq_ab\timing\`.


# Phase 2 — v4 framed format (independent frames)

Same tree, plus `src/v4/`. Every frame is the shared LPC/Rice codec applied
to a slice of the track with an empty reference pool; codec history resets at
each frame start. Default: `-5`, frame_len 16384, all cores.

## Frame size / history reset (47-file set, `--frame N`, all decodes verified)

Reference: v3 L1 (`pack --no-joint -5`) 50.774%, FLAC -8 51.146%.

First attempt — zero history at frame start: overhead ~1/frame_len
(+0.78 pp at 4096, +0.19 pp at 16384, worst file +2.08 pp at 16384). Root cause
on the worst file (narrowband radio, mono i24): the `-5` proxy counted the
unpredictable first `order` samples as residuals and chose a tiny order for the
whole first block (-8 was 663 B/frame cheaper), and those large values sat in
the Rice stream, ruining the first partition's parameter.

Fix (in the v4 bitstream): in a frame's first block the first `order` samples
are stored verbatim (`wbits` u6 + `order` × wbits) with zero placeholders in the
residual stream, and the proxy skips them. Result:

| frame_len | Output | vs v3 L1 | Worst file | Smaller than FLAC -8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 51.186% | +0.412 pp | +0.895 pp | 22/47 |
| 8192 | 50.978% | +0.204 pp | +0.448 pp | 39/47 |
| **16384 (default)** | **50.874%** | **+0.100 pp** | +0.224 pp | **43/47** |
| 32768 | 50.823% | +0.048 pp | +0.111 pp | 44/47 |

Gate (≤ 0.3 pp vs L1): passed at 16384, kept as default (0.37 s per frame at
44.1 kHz — seek and corruption granularity).

## Full WAV/AIFF set (148 files, 1572 MiB, defaults)

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Accepted / verified | 148/148 (WAV: decoded data chunk byte-identical; AIFF: pcm_crc) |
| v4 output | 55.75% (median 58.02%) — v3 full pipeline (`-8` + refs) was 55.29% |
| Encode | 30.5 s total, 51.6 MiB/s (process-level, incl. many small files) |
| Decode | 28.9 s total (single-threaded, streaming) |
| Peak heap | encode ≤ 53.4 MiB, decode ≤ 0.8 MiB (77 MB WAV: 27.9 MiB / 0.6 MiB; v3 needed ~1.6 GiB to encode) |
| Seek | `decode --range` of 0.1 s anywhere in a 400 s file: 9–23 ms wall including process start (`info` alone: 23 ms) |

Against reference codecs, each on the files it accepted (Phase A sizes):

| vs | files | v4 | reference | v4 smaller on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLAC -8 | 79 | 54.66% | 54.89% | 61/79 |
| WavPack -hx | 148 | 55.75% | 56.81% | 92/148 |
| Monkey's Audio -c4000 | 148 | 55.75% | 64.12% | 103/148 |
| TAK -p4m | 48 | 50.91% | 49.87% | 3/48 |
| OptimFROG extranew-light | 73 | 53.98% | 51.33% | 1/73 |

v4 vs WavPack by input type: int WAV 39/59, float WAV 42/63, extensible WAV
11/20, AIFF 0/6 (78.02% vs 77.53%).
